After you mark Death’s Door, you will linger there for a single watch afterwards. If no healing is administered within the span of a watch, someone at Death’s Door will die . If someone dies, there is no return. Death is the final adventure. - Anyone dying in the Underworld rises as an undead—a zombie (if their body is intact) or a wraith (if their body is destroyed). See Zombie for information on zombies and see Wraith for wraiths. While at Death’s Door, a poultice may be applied to forestall doom. Having a poultice applied allows you to test Wands to survive. This test has favor if the person applying the poultice has an applicable medical motif. - On a success, you gain consciousness, mark Stressed, and clear the Death’s Door condition. - On a failure, you die. At the next watch, your body will rise as a zombie. - On a great failure, you die and instantly rise as a zombie. While at Death’s Door, anything—alchemy, magic, or talent—that grants the Heal effect will save your life. - If Healed, you gain consciousness, mark Stressed, and clear the Death’s Door condition.

413.title: New Adventurers
413.breadcrumb: Chapter 7: The Challenge Phase › New Adventurers
413.body: Ultra-fast character creation Here’s a solution if you want to make adventurer creation even faster in the middle of session: - Select your path and your kith and kin. Write down your kin talent. Choose one talent from your path. Name your adventurer. Leave everything else blank for now. - When a question comes up of “Do I have any rope?” or “What’s my Cups score?”, decide at that moment what the answer is. Until that question is raised, your adventurer sheet exists in a Heisenberg uncertainty principle bubble. When the game’s fiction would collapse the uncertainty, write the answer down on your adventurer sheet. - When the session is over and you have time, go ahead and flesh out your adventurer using the normal rules from chapter 2. Adventurer death is a feature not a bug. Victories are hollow when there is no threat of failure. The fact that death is on the line makes each hard-won victory precious. If your adventurer dies, make a new one to rejoin the action using the Call to Adventure rules. These rules are purposefully quick and simple. Skip the bits that involve telling stories so you can get back into the game as quickly as possible. If you’ve died in the middle of a session, the GM should find some plausible excuse for your new adventurer to be added into the scene as soon as you finish creating them. Everybody at the table should be tolerant of whatever leaps of logic it takes to make this happen, but with a little finesse it shouldn’t ruin anybody’s immersion. Your guild-mates can perform the Hold a Funeral City Action later to give your new adventurer a portion of your dead adventurer’s XP (Commission Craft).

414.title: Example Challenge Phase
414.breadcrumb: Chapter 7: The Challenge Phase › Example Challenge Phase
414.body: Initiative strategies One benefit of moving first is it allows you to reveal higher Initiative cards by attacking them early in the round. Later in the round, you can make more informed decisions. A guild named the Steel-Clad Snakes has encountered six goblin raiders in a long, dark hallway in the Castle of Crossed Destinies. The GM drew a random Disposition for the goblins (Social Encounters & Disposition) and found them to be argumentative (i.e., angry). The guild talked to the goblins and found out that they were hired to guard the lair of a sphinx, currently elsewhere. The guild has business in the chambers beyond the goblins and the goblins are unwilling to let them pass. Diplomatic relations break down. The guild consists of Daria the shaman (orc, Path of Wands), Fergus Crowell the alchemist (human, Path of Cups), and Chirm the acrobat (a wood elf assassin, Path of Pentacles).

415.title: Step 0
415.breadcrumb: Chapter 7: The Challenge Phase › Example Challenge Phase › Step 0
415.body: First, the GM sets the scene and clarifies the mechanical aspects of the Challenge. GM: OK, so there’s a hallway, like 15’ long, stretching out in front of you. It’s in darkness, and narrow, only big enough for one person to walk abreast. At the end of the hallway is a foyer, sort of a vestibule. It’s somewhat large, about 15’ x 20’. The six goblins you’re arguing with are encamped there. They have a little fire going, which is filling the upper section with smoke and blackening the wall. Also, the goblins have simple weapons, like bows and daggers drawn. Behind the goblins there is a closed wooden door. Last, in the hallway you hear a slow “swsh swsh” sound. You see a huge, swinging blade at the end of a pendulum bisecting the hallway. So, right now you guys have one torch between the three of you. You can see the end of the chamber at the end of the hall because the goblins have a fire going. There are basically three zones—your room, the hallway, and the goblins’ foyer. To get past the pendulum blade, you’ll need to use an Avoid action. I mean, you can move through the hall zone by playing a Pentacles card, but the total value for that action is going to be compared to the pendulum’s secret Initiative score. If you don’t beat the blade’s Initiative, you’re going to be wounded by the pendulum—and it looks pretty gnarly. Do you guys have any questions before we get started? Chirm: Wait, so, goblins are like… little baby orcs, right? GM: Yeah. They’re like the orc pupal stage. Chirm: So, are they sentient? Daria: I’m an orc. Would I know this? GM: Daria, you would know that goblins are your first stage of life. They’re sentient but stupid, way more driven by instinct. I mean, they’re like little, feral, rival adventurers. Daria: So, I’m about to be a baby killer. Great. GM: Hey that’s up to you. Any other questions? No? OK, everybody draw cards.

416.title: Step 1
416.breadcrumb: Chapter 7: The Challenge Phase › Example Challenge Phase › Step 1
416.body: The players draw 4 cards each from the minor arcana deck. Daria gets these cards: II of Swords, VII of Wands, IX of Wands, King of Pentacles Fergus gets these cards: X of Cups, X of Swords, Page of Wands, the Fool Chirm gets these cards: V of Swords, V of Wands, Ace of Cups, Page of Pentacles The GM reasons that the pendulum blade is basically going to be treated as separate enemy, so they draw 7 cards from the major arcana deck: the 3 default cards, +1 card for each enemy (+2 cards total), +1 card because the enemies outnumber the adventurers, and +1 card because there are twice as many enemies as adventurers. The GM gets these cards: The Emperor \[IV], The Lovers \[VI], The Chariot \[VII], Justice \[XI], Death \[XIII], The Moon \[XVIII], The Sun \[XIX] The GM reorders their hand so that the cards are sequential just for ease of use. The GM notes that The Emperor [IV ], The Lovers \[VI], The Chariot \[VII], Justice \[XI], and Death \[XIII] are lesser dooms, whereas The Moon \[XVIII] and The Sun \[XIX] are greater dooms.

417.title: Step 2
417.breadcrumb: Chapter 7: The Challenge Phase › Example Challenge Phase › Step 2
417.body: Each player plays 1 card facedown for Initiative. - Daria plays the King of Pentacles. - Fergus plays the Page of Wands. - Chirm plays a V of Wands. The GM plays 1 card for Initiative per enemy: one for the goblins and one for the pendulum. The GM rationalizes that the goblins are aggressive and stupid, and so plays their lowest card (The Emperor [IV ]). They then play a middling card, The Chariot \[VII], for the pendulum, saving their higher cards for later mischief. The GM then begins counting upwards to see who takes the first action. GM: OK, everybody have their Initiatives down? OK. 1… 2… 3… 4…

418.title: Step 3
418.breadcrumb: Chapter 7: The Challenge Phase › Example Challenge Phase › Step 3
418.body: At the count of 4, the GM flips over the goblin’s Initiative and takes their turn. GM: OK, I go on 4. The goblins have their weapons out, so they’re going to go ahead and take potshots at you with their bows. There’s six of them, but only half of them have bows out and drawn, so let’s just say one attack per person. The GM elects to use the Attack action. They play Justice \[XI] and—since it’s their turn—adds the goblins’ Swords 4 for a total of 15. GM: Does a 15 hit everybody ? Now that they’ve been attacked, each player flips over their Initiative cards. - Daria’s King has a value of 14. - Fergus’s Page has a value of 11. - Chirm has a 5. Daria: They’re shooting down at us from a narrow hallway, right? Can I duck behind the wall and get a little cover? GM: Sure, that makes sense. You all can, in fact. I’ll take disfavor to my shot. That’ll put my total at 12. I think that hits everybody but you, Daria. Daria: Nice. Fergus hasn’t suffered any damage so far during this Crawl and so marks Staggered. Chirm is already Staggered. She is wearing light armor and a helm, so she Notches the helm. Helms can only absorb 1 Wound, so it is Destroyed. Chirm’s player erases the helm from her sheet. The GM puts their played card on top of the major arcana discard pile.

419.title: Step 4
419.breadcrumb: Chapter 7: The Challenge Phase › Example Challenge Phase › Step 4
419.body: GM: OK. Minor actions on my turn? Fergus: Uh, can I throw a bomb at the goblins from here? GM: There’s a hallway with a big blade in the middle of it. You’d have to basically fastball it back there. If you play a value less than the pendulum’s Initiative, it’ll bounce off of it and explode in the hallway. Fergus: Fuck it. I’m going to try. GM: Sure, but I’m going to impose disfavor since I took it. The goblins can also duck a little behind the cover of the wall. Chirm: Once Fergus throws the bomb, I’m going to run down the hallway too. GM: OK. So, play an Avoid card and try to beat the pendulum’s Initiative. Fergus, you go ahead and play your Use Item card, too. Fergus plays a X of Cups to Use Item as a minor action. Chirm plays a Page of Pentacles to Avoid as a minor action. Because these are minor actions, neither player adds anything to the card’s value. Fergus: With disfavor, total is 7. Chirm: I’ll play a Page of Pentacles. My total is 11. The GM flips over the Initiative of the pendulum trap, revealing that it’s a VII. GM: The pendulum’s Initiative is a 7. Fergus, you tied but ties will go to the attacker here. You both make it past the pendulum. Fergus, what kind of bomb was it? Fergus: It’s the spider sac bomb. Because the Use Item action’s value is greater than the goblins’ Initiative, the bomb hits one of the goblins. GM: Great. So, when you throw the bomb, it explodes and quickly spreads out like a web thrown by Spiderman. One of the goblins is stuck to the wall. What stats did we say that it had? Fergus: Anything stuck is Rooted and attacks against webbed creatures have favor. GM: Dope. Chirm, you enter the goblins’ vestibule. You are surrounded by six goblins. One is stuck to the wall by webbing. Any other minor actions? Daria: I’ll fire back with my archwood wand. GM: Cool. Don’t forget the disfavor. Because the use of archwood wands is unlocked through the talent Gramarye, Daria can use a Wand card as an Attack action. Daria plays a VII of Wands to Attack. Her Attack has disfavor (–3), so the total is 4. GM: What’s your total? Daria: A 4. The goblins don’t have shields do they? GM: No, they don’t. It meets their Initiative, so it hits. The goblin yelps in pain from the arcane blast. The GM notes that goblins have HD 2/1, so they tick off 1 Defense damage on a random goblin, reducing it to HD 2/0. The Challenge sequence returns to step 3 as players continue to take turns.

420.title: Step 3
420.breadcrumb: Chapter 7: The Challenge Phase › Example Challenge Phase › Step 3
420.body: GM: Any other minor actions? No? OK. I was on 4. 5… 6… 7… Chirm: Sorry, 5 is me. OK, so I’m up there with the goblins, right? GM: You sure are, and they look mean. Chirm: OK, I’m going to stab the one that’s in the web. Does that give favor? GM: Yep. Chirm plays an Ace of Cups to perform an Attack. Because it’s her turn, she can play a card of any suit and she adds her Swords 2. Because she has favor, she adds +3. The total is 6. The situation also triggers the dagger’s special ability . Chirm: OK, so, since I have favor, the total is 6. Wait. I’m wielding a dagger, and you said the goblin’s Rooted. So that’s Piercing damage, right? GM: Nice. Yes. 6 hits. The GM notes down one Piercing wound, which is subtracted directly from the goblin's Health. That goblin is now HD 1/1. Chirm: The goblin’s still alive? GM: Yes, that one goblin is still alive, but looks like you got it in the ribs.

421.title: Step 4
421.breadcrumb: Chapter 7: The Challenge Phase › Example Challenge Phase › Step 4
421.body: Once Chirm has taken her turn, the phase goes back to step 4. GM: Minor actions on 5? Uh, I think I’m going to make one. The goblins are going to Attack… anybody else? Daria: I’m going to swap out my wand for a magic component on my belt . Daria plays a II of Swords to Pull Item from Belt. Neither the suit nor the value matter for this action. GM: OK. So. I think the goblins are really pissed at all the things you’re doing to them, and one wielding a dagger stabs towards Chirm. Because there are at least four goblins active in this zone, they’re going to Attack with favor and do Piercing damage. The GM plays Death \[XIII] as an Attack. The goblins gain favor and deal Piercing damage by outnumbering the adventurer (per “Mob rule,” see Play Initiative). To activate one of the goblins’ greater dooms—Poison—they also play the Moon \[XVIII]. If this Attack hits, the goblin’s dagger will inflict a poison-related affliction. GM: Crowding around you with their tiny shards of murder, one goblin swings at Chirm with a poisoned dagger. With a 13 versus your 5, I’m going to hit and… Fergus: NOT SO FAST! Fergus throws down the Fool and the X of Swords. He intends to use the Dodge action for Chirm. Because using the Fool gives the player an extra turn, Fergus can use a card of any suit and add his attribute to the action’s total value. Fergus: I interrupt! I’m going to play a Dodge action for Chirm. The GM knows that Dodging for someone in another zone isn’t 100% rules-as-written but is open to the idea of making an exception if they can make a case for it. It’s a cool idea and they want to reward Fergus’s creativity. GM: Oh my God that rules! OK, but you have to tell me, like, exactly what you’re doing. Normally you can only play defensive cards for folks in your same zone. What are you doing to help Chirm dodge? Fergus: I yell, like, “Look out behind you,” right as the goblin stabs towards her . GM: OK! Sure, that can work. So, what’s your total Initiative now, Chirm ? Chirm: How much do I add ? Fergus: So, the Fool counts as my turn so I can add my Pentacles. The card’s a 10, plus my Pentacles of 2, for a plus 12 to your Initiative. Chirm: Plus my Initiative of 5, so 17 total. GM: The goblin has a 13, which is 16 with favor. It just barely misses you as you dodge out of the way! Incredible. OK, so that was Chirm’s turn. What count were we on? Chirm: We were on 5.

422.title: Step 3
422.breadcrumb: Chapter 7: The Challenge Phase › Example Challenge Phase › Step 3
422.body: GM: OK, so 6… 7… 8… 9… 10… Page… Fergus: Page is me, but I’m out of cards. GM: OK, so we’ll move on. I think Daria is the only person who hasn’t had a turn yet. Daria? Daria: I’m going to Banter with the goblins. GM: What exactly are you saying, and what card are you going to play? Daria plays a IX of Wands to Banter. Since this is Daria’s turn, she doesn’t necessarily need to use a Wands suit to Banter; this is coincidental. Because it’s her turn, Daria also adds her Wands 4 to the attempt for a total value of 13. Daria: I speak with the showmanship of a shaman who comes from an oral storytelling culture and is used to leading public rites, saying, “Our power cannot be contested. We are mightier than you. Gather up your miserable little lives and run while you still can.” GM: Total value? Daria: 13. The GM quickly consults the Morale rules (Wands actions) and decides that the goblins are at least “wary.” That puts their Morale at 10. The 13 succeeds in changing their Disposition. The goblins move their Disposition from “Angry” to “Afraid.” GM: OK, the goblins seem alarmed. They start clawing at their friends in the web, and one of them begins to open the door behind them. They seem like they want to escape. Minor actions on this step? I think the goblins are going to try and start to run.

423.title: Step 4
423.breadcrumb: Chapter 7: The Challenge Phase › Example Challenge Phase › Step 4
423.body: Chirm: I want to wrestle one of the fleeing goblins into the pendulum . Chirm plays a V of Swords to Roughhouse. Because this is a minor action, the total is 5. Chirm: Because I have Fight Dirty mastered, I’m spending a Swords card as a Roughhouse action. GM: So your total is 5? OK, describe what you’re doing. Chirm: Since the goblins are so small I’m just going to pick up one and, like, throw it down the hallway. GM: That works. The GM reasons that this applies the Displace effect, which is well within Fight Dirty’s purview. The GM had secretly determined that the pendulum blade would deal 2 Piercing Wounds. They had broadcast its deadliness in their original description of the scene, and so ticks off two points on a goblin’s Health. This kills the goblin. GM: The pendulum blade catches him in midair and savagely wounds him. The goblin is down on the ground, bleeding out. He’s out of the fight.

424.title: Step 5
424.breadcrumb: Chapter 7: The Challenge Phase › Example Challenge Phase › Step 5
424.body: Since Daria is the last person to act, the Challenge continues to step 5 (end the round) after the minor actions are resolved. Since the Fool was drawn, both the minor and major arcana decks are reshuffled. Practically speaking, most Challenges end once one side attempts to disengage. If the players wanted to press their advantage and the GM wanted to continue using the Challenge Phase, play would continue: - Any facedown cards would remain on the table. - Step 0 would begin by having the GM restate the current location and status of all combatants, reminding all players of the special rules in effect. - At step 1, everybody would get a new hand of Challenge cards.

425.title: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase
425.body: ‘There is food in the wild,’ said Strider; ‘berry, root, and herb; and I have some skill as a hunter at need. You need not be afraid of starving before winter comes. But gathering and catching food is long and weary work, and we need haste.’” – The Fellowship of the Ring, J. R. R. Tolkien There is some common wisdom about making encampments in the Underworld encapsulated in a song. The song has become so popular in guild-haunted taverns that it has trickled out into the general population. This song is usually called the “Camping Song,” and it’s sung to an ancient melody. The Camping Song runs thus: O! Underneath hill and barrow go Where cold sun’s absent Five rivers flow In the Spires, want not for light Fallen wood kindles Unwanted sight In the Ruin, a quiet bower Ring with garlic Feast th’ vampires Isles in Moat, ships land upon First make fire Beware Fastitocalon! In the Castle, close tight the door Iron spikes for locks For beds, stone floor In Inverted Castle, beware the Worm The mazes shift And even He will turn

426.title: The Flow of the Camp Phase
426.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase
426.body: The pace of travel Rations are the resource that drive the Camp Phase. As such, the opportunity to perform Camp Actions is dependent on the guild’s ability to manage their inventory. Likewise, because charged Bonds drive step 4 of the Camp Phase (Recovery), you have an impetus to avoid striking camp too often: only after a good exchange of role-playing scenes. When adventuring has left the guild injured, miserable, and expended, they put down their packs and set up camp. During the Camp Phase, everyone rests and recovers from the stresses of the Crawl. The Camp Phase runs thus:

427.title: 1. Camp Actions
427.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 1. Camp Actions
427.body: Set up camp and perform a Camp Action.

428.title: 2. Break bread
428.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 2. Break bread
428.body: Consume a ration. If you can't do this, check the Stressed condition.

429.title: 3. No rest for the wicked
429.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 3. No rest for the wicked
429.body: The GM checks for any random Camp events.

430.title: 4. Recovery
430.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 4. Recovery
430.body: Automatically refill your allotment of lore bids and clear the Staggered condition. For every charged Bond you burn, heal 1 Wound or regain 1 point of Resolve. - If you are Stressed, you must burn a charged Bond to erase this condition first. Being Stressed prevents you from healing Wounds or recovering Resolve. - If you are Injured, you must burn a Bond to clear this condition before you can heal any Wounded talents.

431.title: 5. End of Camp Phase
431.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 5. End of Camp Phase
431.body: Check to make sure you have at least two of the following: bedroll, tent, or fire. If you don’t, you wake up Stressed.

432.title: 1. Camp Actions
432.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 1. Camp Actions
432.body: Each adventurer has the opportunity to undertake one meaningful activity. ^camp-actions This is not an exhaustive list of Camp Actions, but a structure for handling common requests. GMs and players should work together to expand the list using these rules as a template.

433.title: Fellowship
433.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 1. Camp Actions › Fellowship
433.body: Pick a guild-mate and engage in a role-play with them. - Share a memory. Talk about their quests. Ask about their childhood; tell about yours. - End the conversation meaningfully so that the table knows you're done talking. - At the end of this exchange, you both charge your Bonds with each other.

434.title: Fletch Arrows
434.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 1. Camp Actions › Fletch Arrows
434.body: Spend some time looking for and crafting shafts for your recovered arrowheads. Refill your quiver of arrows or bolts to twelve.

435.title: Hunt
435.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 1. Camp Actions › Hunt
435.body: Scout outside of camp to try and find some game that looks halfway edible. You must have a missile weapon to go hunting. Test Swords . - If you succeed, you return with 1 ration’s worth of food (about the size of a rat). - On a great success, you bring back a large beast capable of providing a meal for the entire guild (like a dire rat). - If you fail, no game is found. - Great failures trigger a Challenge Phase. - Hunted game needs to be prepared in order to be eaten. This requires cooking gear. - Preserving the meat as rations requires salt. - The GM will tell you what sort of food is available; you’re responsible for deciding how picky you are about rations.

436.title: Patrol
436.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 1. Camp Actions › Patrol
436.body: Keep guard, patrolling around your encampment and setting up assault counter-measures. If an adventurer takes the Patrol action, the GM draws twice on the Meatgrinder table and takes a non-random encounter result if available during step 3 of the Camp Phase (No Rest for the Wicked).

437.title: Read a Book
437.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 1. Camp Actions › Read a Book
437.body: Read a book that you’re carrying with you. Ask the GM one question related to the subject matter of the book. They will tell you what the book says about it. - This operates like a lore bid, but based on information found in the book.

438.title: Rest and Recover
438.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 1. Camp Actions › Rest and Recover
438.body: Wrap your blankets around you and try to sleep through your cold sweats. If you are suffering from an affliction (Afflictions), you must take this action to spend charged Bonds in order to stave off the sickness.

439.title: Scout Ahead
439.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 1. Camp Actions › Scout Ahead
439.body: Walk quietly outside of camp, peer down hallways, and listen at adjacent doors. If you scout around, you might be able to learn something interesting about the terrain. Test Pentacles . - If you succeed, the GM will give you a hint about some encounters in the nearby rooms or tell you what sort of creatures frequent here. If you’re adjacent to special rooms, you'll learn about them. - A great success will give you as much information about what is nearby as the GM can give. - If you fail, you retreat without learning anything new. - Great failures trigger a Challenge Phase.

440.title: Train
440.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 1. Camp Actions › Train
440.body: Study with a willing guild-mate and learn a talent from them. Your guild-mate must have mastered the skill in questions in order to train others. This takes both of your Camp Actions, and they get nothing from the exchange. - Invest XP into the talent they are teaching you. - Prepare as many uses of that talent as you have XP invested. See Talents for the full rules on training talents.

441.title: Update Maps
441.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 1. Camp Actions › Update Maps
441.body: Spend some time updating your map and charting your course. Mark down the rooms that you’ve traveled through since your last Camp Phase. These are your mapped rooms . You can travel through two mapped rooms per watch . This allows you to travel through two mapped rooms per Meatgrinder event instead of one.

442.title: Use an Item
442.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 1. Camp Actions › Use an Item
442.body: If you’re carrying an item that’s usable during the Camp Phase (e.g., a tinker’s kit) you may use it during this step.

443.title: Use a Talent
443.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 1. Camp Actions › Use a Talent
443.body: If you have a talent that’s usable during the Camp Phase (e.g., Beast Master, Bookworm, War Stories, etc.) you may use it during this step.

444.title: 2. Break bread
444.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 2. Break bread
444.body: Starving In general terms, a person can endure about three weeks of starvation before dying. Let us assume that “dying from starvation” is a fringe case in His Majesty the Worm . It’s much more likely that adventurers will run low on rations during the Crawl and need to endure a few days of empty bellies. If this is your second Camp Phase without consuming rations, you begin to starve. If you are starving, skip steps 4 and 5 of the Camp Phase. You cannot burn charged Bonds or regain lore bids while starving. Once Camp Actions have been declared, the guild settles down to eat a meal together. Every adventurer must consume 1 ration at this step or become Stressed . If you didn’t eat last time either, you begin to starve (see sidebar). ^break-bread Each animal companion must also consume 1 animal feed . Animal companions that are not fed become weak and cannot be commanded. In essence, rations power the entire Camp Phase, and thus enable healing and recovery. Managing your inventory to balance an appropriate number of rations vs. other adventuring gear is, therefore, a crucial consideration. The GM can use this step to introduce a role-playing prompt, see Running the Camp Phase.

445.title: 3. No rest for the wicked
445.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 3. No rest for the wicked
445.body: While the adventurers rest, the Underworld continues to go about its sinister business. The GM should draw on the Meatgrinder table for the dungeon the adventurers are camping in (Meatgrinder). Random events like rainstorms and rising fog will add flavor to the Camp Phase, but probably won’t impose any special rules. If a random encounter is pulled, the Camp Phase is interrupted by a Challenge. It is assumed that adventurers are taking turns guarding the camp while they rest. If a random encounter occurs, the GM should randomly determine who’s on watch. An easy way to do this is to look at the top card of the minor arcana discard pile: the suit displayed corresponds to the path of the adventurer on guard. If there are multiple adventurers of the same path, odd cards target the player to the GM’s left, even cards target the player to the GM’s right. The adventurer on guard tests Cups . - If successful, the alarm is raised before the random encounter finds the encampment. The guild has a brief period of time to prepare. - If the test of fate is a failure, the guild is surprised. - A guild caught asleep is very vulnerable—nobody is wearing armor or actively wielding weapons. - See Special rules for the rules about surprise. If one of the players has performed the Patrol action, the GM draws twice on the Meatgrinder table and chooses a non-encounter result if possible. A Challenge only occurs if both cards reveal a random encounter—the GM chooses which one to use. Once the Challenge is resolved, the Camp Phase continues on to step 4.

446.title: 4. Recovery
446.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 4. Recovery
446.body: During the Camp Phase, you may burn any charged Bonds to clear the Stressed condition, clear the Injured condition, heal one Wounded talent, or regain 1 Resolve. This leaves the Bond uncharged. ^recovery - If you are Stressed, you must burn a charge to erase this condition before you can clear any other conditions. - If you are Injured, you must burn a charge to erase this condition before you can heal any Wounded talents. If you are not Stressed at the end of this step, you automatically clear the Staggered condition. If your animal companion or familiar is Injured, you may burn a charged Bond to clear this condition. If your animal companion or familiar is only Staggered, they automatically clear this condition. At the end of this step, refill all of your lore bids up to four (the max).

447.title: 5. End of Camp Phase
447.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › The Flow of the Camp Phase › 5. End of Camp Phase
447.body: If you’re encamped and not sleeping in a shelter, you need two of the following: ^end-of-camp-phase - bedroll - tent - fire If you don’t have at least two of these, you wake up Stressed at the end of the Camp Phase. Once these steps have been completed, the Crawl Phase resumes.

448.title: Optional Rules: Overland Travel
448.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › Optional Rules: Overland Travel
448.body: Most of His Majesty the Worm is focused on dungeon-crawling in the mythic Underworld. It abstracts concerns of food, time, and distance into the flow of the Camp and Crawl Phases. If your game takes place in a setting where the sun shines, you might want a system that adds an additional layer of logistics to travel. If this is the case, use these rules. Each day is divided into three watches . Each watch takes about eight hours. Using these optional rules, timekeeping becomes important. After three watches, a new day dawns. The GM should step through the calendar as they pass day by day. For each watch, follow this procedure:

449.title: 1. Choose action
449.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › Optional Rules: Overland Travel › 1. Choose action
449.body: The guild chooses a single overland action to take.

450.title: 2. Meatgrinder
450.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › Optional Rules: Overland Travel › 2. Meatgrinder
450.body: The GM draws on their Meatgrinder table for a random event or encounter.

451.title: 3. Set the scene
451.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › Optional Rules: Overland Travel › 3. Set the scene
451.body: The GM describes the random encounter in the context of the hex the guild is traveling in. The players and the GM play out the scene, and when it’s over, the GM calls for a new overland action to be chosen. “The cave you fear to enter holds the treasure you seek.” – Joseph Campbell

452.title: Overland actions
452.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › Optional Rules: Overland Travel › Overland actions
452.body: Each watch, the guild can perform one of the following overland actions. It’s important to note that, using these optional rules, step 1 of the Camp Phase is separated from steps 2–5.

453.title: Camp Action
453.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › Optional Rules: Overland Travel › Overland actions › Camp Action
453.body: Each adventurer can choose any of the Camp Actions listed on pages 137–139 to perform.

454.title: Encamp
454.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › Optional Rules: Overland Travel › Overland actions › Encamp
454.body: The guild beds down for the night. Run through steps 2–5 of the Camp Phase.

455.title: Explore
455.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › Optional Rules: Overland Travel › Overland actions › Explore
455.body: Look for interesting things within a hex. The GM informs the guild of any notable features, lairs, terrain, or spoor that are discoverable within the area they’re in.

456.title: Interact
456.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › Optional Rules: Overland Travel › Overland actions › Interact
456.body: Interact with a special feature or location (e.g., exploring a dungeon or visiting a hamlet).

457.title: Travel
457.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › Optional Rules: Overland Travel › Overland actions › Travel
457.body: The guild travels from their current hex into an adjacent one. If there are clear roads, they can move +1 hex. If everyone in the guild is riding, they can move another +1 hex. Under the eye of the sun, questions of exhaustion and hunger come into play more than under the standard rules. Characters who fail to Encamp once per day become Exhausted—all tests and all Challenge Actions are made with disfavor until they Encamp again.

458.title: Example Camp Phase
458.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › Example Camp Phase
458.body: After an encounter with a cyclops, a guild named the Finders checks in with each other and decides to bed down for the night. They are in the Spires—a wooded dungeon——and feel that the forest gives them a secluded place to rest. The guild consists of Phynn Heartsbane the serpent cultist (human, Path of Swords), Envyrie the goth assassin (dark elf, Path of Pentacles), and Byron Cartwright the enterprising trickster (halfling, Path of Pentacles). The guild is generally bruised and broken. They hope that a peaceful Camp Phase will allow them to continue their delving.

459.title: Step 1. Camp Actions
459.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › Example Camp Phase › Step 1. Camp Actions
459.body: GM: OK, so what are you doing? Phynn: I’m repairing my armor. Phynn’s iron chainmail suffered terribly in the combat with the cyclops, so he elects to Use an Item (a tinker’s kit) and repair his armor. He repairs his iron armor by 1 Notch. Envyrie: I’ll scout ahead and see if there’s anything interesting nearby. GM: Go ahead and test Pentacles. Envyrie tests Pentacles and draws a 7. Envyrie has Pentacles 4, so the total is 11. Thinking this a safe bet, she pushes fate and succeeds by drawing a 5 for a new total of 16. The GM looks at their map and describes the most interesting nearby room. GM: OK, as you go scouting, you come into a new section of the woods. You find a group of orcs encamped around a burned section of the forest—the smell of woodsmoke is still thick in the air. At the center of the burning is a giant dragon’s skeleton. The orcs appear to be worshiping it, or at least having some sort of religious ceremony akin to a Baptist revival near it. Envyrie: Envyrie returns to camp and tells her friends what she saw. GM: Byron, what are you doing? Byron: Byron’s going to continue to recover from the takalashi jelly. Byron has been trying to recover from his addiction to takalashi jelly, an affliction (Afflictions). The GM has decided privately that addiction to takalashi jelly has two stages, similar to black honey. They decided that stage 2 requires 1 charge to cure, stage 1 requires 5 charges to cure. Byron takes the Rest and Recover action. Byron’s affliction is currently at stage 2. He currently has charged Bonds with both Envyrie and Phynn, and elects to burn one to treat his addiction. This moves him down to stage 1. GM: Great. Just to help us all picture the scene, what does the camp look like as you set it up? Phynn: There stuff for a campfire? GM: Yeah, plenty of deadfall wood in the Spires. Phynn: We light a campfire with the wood. I pull my bedroll up to the fire to keep warm. Envyrie: I’ll share my tent with Byron so he has a quiet place to detox. GM: Cool. The fire casts your shadows broadly onto the giant trees that surround you. It crackles merrily. The sound of the tree frogs is all but drowned out by the droning of the terrible locusts that you’ve been encountering.

460.title: Step 2: Break bread
460.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › Example Camp Phase › Step 2: Break bread
460.body: GM: Everybody eating a ration? The entire party nods and erases 1 ration from each of their packs. Because the session only has a few minutes before the group needs to stop playing and get back to their lives, the GM elects not to introduce a campfire discussion.

461.title: Step 3: No rest for the wicked
461.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › Example Camp Phase › Step 3: No rest for the wicked
461.body: Because nobody performed the Patrol action, the GM only draws one card from the major arcana deck and gets the Emperor [IV ]. The GM looks at the Meatgrinder table for the dungeon to check what event is tied to this result. They determine it isn’t a random encounter, so they describe the night passing quietly.

462.title: Step 4: Recovery
462.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › Example Camp Phase › Step 4: Recovery
462.body: GM: The night passes without incident. Everybody burn charged Bonds to recover. Each player now has the opportunity to burn charged Bonds to recover. All of the players automatically refill their lore bid uses. - Phynn has charged Bonds with both of his guildmates. He is Stressed, Staggered, and has one Wounded talent. - Because Phynn is Stressed, he must clear this condition first. He burns one charge to do so. - Because he is no longer Stressed, Staggered is cleared automatically. - Phynn then burns his second charge to cure his Wounded talent. - Phynn begins the next Crawl Phase with no conditions. - Envyrie has no charged Bonds. She is Staggered and has one Wounded talent. - Because Envyrie isn’t Stressed, Staggered is cleared automatically. - Because she has no charged Bonds, she can’t do anything else during this step. - Byron has one remaining charged Bond (he burned his first during Step 1). He is Staggered, Injured, and has two Wounded talents. - Because Byron isn’t Stressed, Staggered is cleared automatically. - Byron burns his charge to clear Injured because it is very dangerous. Another Wound would knock him to Death’s Door. - Byron begins the next Crawl Phase with two Wounded talents, but at least he is no longer Injured.

463.title: Step 5: End of Camp Phase
463.breadcrumb: Chapter 8: The Camp Phase › Example Camp Phase › Step 5: End of Camp Phase
463.body: GM: OK, everybody done recovering? I heard you had a fire. Did everybody have somewhere to sleep? The entire party nods. GM: OK, everybody begins the next Crawl well rested. Nobody is Stressed. Unfortunately, Byron, your affliction is going to automatically progress to the next level. You are back at stage 2 of your jelly addiction.

464.title: Chapter 9: The City Phase
464.body: “Of that Byzantine Empire, the universal verdict of history is that it constitutes, with scarcely an exception, the most thoroughly base and despicable form that civilisation has yet assumed. ... They possessed knowledge; they had continually before them the noble literature of ancient Greece, instinct with the loftiest heroism; but that literature, which afterwards did so much to revivify Europe, could fire the degenerate Greeks with no spark or semblance of nobility. The history of the Empire is a monotonous story of the intrigues of priests, eunuchs, and women, of poisonings, of conspiracies, of uniform ingratitude, of perpetual fratricides.” – History of European Morals, William Edward Hartpole Lecky The City is the center of the Wide World; the navel of creation. It is at a crossroads, twin-faced, staring east and west. It is equidistant to Alfheim, the Steppes of the Dragons, and the mountainous Delvings of Eight Cities. In majesty it is unmatched. In wealth, unequaled. Anything can be bought in the City for the right price. The most skilled craftsmen in the Wide World perfect their arts in the City. For the very rich, even the powers of the Underworld might be traded. These wealthy patrons tempt guilds of adventurers to brave life and limb for the treasures hidden underneath the great metropolis. The City has been claimed by many kith and kin, but today it is the seat of humanity. A handful of powerful human houses struggle continuously for power. Enclaves of distant powers and races seize toeholds in the City and pursue their strange designs in their embassies. Like skin, it is made of folded-over layers. Each era of the City can be found buried below the others. Dig down into your cellar and find the potsherds, runestones, idols, rusted machinery, diaries, lamps, and bones of those who came before. Like skin, it has scars. Terrible pits boring holes into the Underworld—blighted cankers on a beautiful face.

465.title: The Flow of the City Phase
465.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase
465.body: The City is social The City contains an untold multitude of factions, social clubs, hierarchies, royal families, anarchist collectives, sports teams, mystery cults, underground scenes, crime syndicates, etc. They want what the guild has: treasure, expertise, and a lack of self-preservation. The guild wants what these organizations have: influence, power, wealth…sure, but also fancy clothes, useful rumors, interesting friends, cool home bases, etc. When the guild returns to civilization, laden with treasure and light on supplies, the City Phase begins. The City Phase is an opportunity to pursue long-term goals, research the next steps of the quest, and restock supplies before returning to the Stygian depths. This chapter details what players need to know about the City Phase. Advice for the GM for running the City Phase is found in chapter 10. Procedures for the GM to flesh out a City are found in Appendix D: City Creation. Here is the summary of the City Phase:

466.title: 1. Death and taxes
466.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 1. Death and taxes
466.body: Each player turns in 50% of carried gold coins to the black-armored All-Watch as guild tax.

467.title: 2. Noteworthy deeds
467.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 2. Noteworthy deeds
467.body: Erase the oldest deed on your roster. As a group, write the most notable accomplishments from your last Crawl on your guild roster.

468.title: 3. City Events
468.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 3. City Events
468.body: The GM draws for a random event on their City Event table.

469.title: 4. Turn in contracts
469.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 4. Turn in contracts
469.body: The guild turns in their contract (if any). Successfully completed contracts provide a monetary reward and 1XP.

470.title: 5. Upkeep
470.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 5. Upkeep
470.body: Each player pays for an upkeep tier. - If you pay no upkeep, you are destitute for this City Phase. You do not refill your pack. - Impoverished upkeep costs 25 gold. - Refill your pack with impoverished-level gear from the Omphalic Market. - Common upkeep costs 50 gold. - Refill your pack with common- or impoverished-level gear from the Omphalic Market. - Burn charges to heal Wounds and clear conditions as per step 4 of the Camp Phase (Recovery) (End of Camp Phase). - Luxurious upkeep costs 100 gold. - Refill your pack with any gear from the Omphalic Market. - Heal all of your Wounds and refresh all your Resolve.

471.title: 6. City Actions
471.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 6. City Actions
471.body: Each player performs a City Action.

472.title: 7. Plan the next Crawl
472.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 7. Plan the next Crawl
472.body: The guild reassembles to talk over next steps as a group. The GM provides a list of possible contracts. Sign up for a contract (or two).

473.title: 8. Restock the Underworld
473.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 8. Restock the Underworld
473.body: Before the next session, the GM restocks the Meatgrinder tables.

474.title: 1. Death and taxes
474.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 1. Death and taxes
474.body: Goddammit, I’m a sovereign citizen! Truth be told, the 50% tax was included in playtests merely as a lark. However, it evoked such a strong response in the playtesters that it was obvious that it had to be kept in the core game. Despite the fact everybody was only moving around imaginary numbers on paper, the players were very keen to avoid taxes. And, in a meaningful way, taxes made going back to the City unappetizing. The City Phase should be rare. High taxes mean that players view returning to the surface as a last resort. When you return through one of the gates of the Underworld, the All-Watch—elite warriors who serve the lord of the City—demand 50% of your guild’s liquid assets as guild tax. ^death-and-taxes Liquid assets mean “gold coins.” The Underworld is full of golden coins marked with pentacles. Non-liquid assets are items of art and extravagance, such as paintings, statues, gems (uncut and cut), books, decorative weapons, jewelry, etc. These are not taken by the All-Watch. This tax was established by the City to pay for the frequent calamities associated with the adventuring guilds. The taxes go into a fund to pay for tavern fights that become fires, engorged slimes brought back to the surface as babies, and the salaries of the All-Watch (to keep them unbribable).

475.title: 2. Noteworthy deeds
475.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 2. Noteworthy deeds
475.body: Historical note You know the song Istanbul by The Four Lads (famously covered by They Might Be Giants)? The question of why the city is called Istanbul has an answer: it is derived from the Greek εις την Πόλιν ( istanbulin ), which simply means “the city.” Constantinople was the place to be in the ancient world, so you needn’t even call it by its formal name. It was simply the city. The name of the city in His Majesty the Worm is merely “the City.” This is its common name (if not its official one). It had other names in the past (even as Constantinople did—Byzantium, New Rome, and Augustus Antonia to name a few), but “the City” is how people refer to it now. What are the City’s past names? Has the current government always been in power? What ancient powers once dwelt here? That’s up to your group to decide. When you return to the City, erase the oldest noteworthy deed on your guild roster. Then, review if your guild has done anything noteworthy since the last City Phase. Everybody at the table can suggest a few things that might qualify as a noteworthy deed. This might include a dungeon lord slain, a new path through the Underworld forged, a piece of prominent architecture destroyed, or a potent relic reclaimed. The GM is the arbiter for what is considered actually noteworthy. ^noteworthy-deeds A guild’s Fame equals the amount of active noteworthy deeds. Your Fame affects the way the GM’s characters treat you: more famous adventurers are given more attention, wanted or unwanted. from the Greek εις την Πόλιν A guild can have up to five active noteworthy deeds at a time. If you would have more than five, choose whichever five seem the most praiseworthy. See Chapter 3: The Guild for a full description of Fame and noteworthy deeds. If you return to the City and have accomplished nothing since your last visit, you erase the oldest deed on your roster and lose 1 Fame accordingly.

476.title: 3. City Events
476.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 3. City Events
476.body: The City is never dull. When you stagger back to the surface, you enter a chaotic metropolis with all its intrigues, politics, and spectacle. ^city-events Before play, the GM should construct a City Events table , detailing potential events that frame the guild’s visit. During this step, the GM draws a major arcana card, consults this table, and interprets the result. The results need not happen instantly. For example, if the GM draws a rumor on the City Events table, they might have a contract-giver or shopkeeper deliver the rumor to the guild through the course of playing out the City Phase. The City Events table should have twenty-one entries and follow this formula: Curiosities (I–V): Curiosities are moments of serendipity. GMs, use these events to inject color into the game. Curiosities create a sense of realness, and are opportunities to demonstrate what kind of City exists in your game. Are curiosity events dark portents like raving madmen calling for repentance under the blood moon or are they bucolic affairs with Punch and Judy puppet shows? Happenings (VI–X): Happenings are events that frame the lives of the residents of the City. These are the saturnalia, feasts, and holy days that break up the wheel of years. Happenings should make the City Phase feel different to the players. Visiting the City during a religious festival is much different than visiting during the normal drudge of days. Rumors (XI–XV): Rumors hint at the contents of the Underworld: treasures, monsters, traps, hazards, and history. Rumors are opportunities to tell lore and define the “story” of the dungeon. Travel events (XVI–XX): Travel events are often things that go wrong in a trip to the City, or a chance to confront the players to make a hard choice. Signs and Portents (XXI): Signs and portents are special events wherein weirdness has spilled out from the Underworld and complicates life in the City. When drawing this result, the GM looks at the top card of the minor arcana discard pile and then consults the Signs and Portents table. Like the Meatgrinder table, the GM should keep the City Events table tidy and fresh, swapping out used entries with new content (see step 8). The next page has an example City Events table to serve as a starting point.

477.title: Example City Events
477.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 3. City Events › Example City Events
477.body: Card City Event :---: --- I [Curiosity] Gross: A bucket of night soil is emptied onto a random adventurer from a high-up window. II [Curiosity] Doggy: A starving dog trails behind the guild, whining. Its ribs stick out and its pink skin is clearly visible through its mangy fur. It licks your hands with a dry, grey tongue. If you feed it, it may follow you. III [Curiosity] An Execution: A crowd gathers to watch a hanging. A tonsured Mythric cultist of middling initiation pronounces a sentence of death on a hooded man for the crime of punching a noble and subsequently loosening the noble’s tooth. To loud applause, the man drops and jerks on the gibbet. IV [Curiosity] Stylite: From his high pillar, a naked stylite pronounces doom down on the adventurer with the highest Wands score. The stylite loudly decries their vices and denounces their escapades as lecherous and murderous. He seems to know a lot about the adventurer, honestly. It would be impressive if it wasn’t so mean and truthful. V [Curiosity] Lick Lick Lick: An old woman, drunk as a skunk, sits in the gutter singing an old- fashioned tune. She doesn’t seem to notice the bloated rat licking her ankles. VI [Happening] Famine: A long winter has left the granaries empty. Food is scarce. You can only buy rations if you maintain a luxurious lifestyle during step 5 (Upkeep). VII [Happening] The Ecstasy of St. Naos: By far the biggest party day of the year: like St. Patrick’s and Mardi Gras had a baby. The City is shut down. The only City Action the adventurers can perform during step 6 (City Actions) is Carousing. VIII [Happening] The Coronation of Maiden Wisdom: One of the highest holy days in the Mythric calendar, charity is given generously during this time. Rates for upkeep are reduced: impoverished is 15g, common is 25g, and luxurious is 50g. IX [Happening] The Feast of the Constellations: During the Feast of the Constellations, the pious of the Cult fast. By custom and law, all taverns are closed and the drinking of alcohol is punished by use of a scold’s bridle. Carousing cannot be performed during this phase. X [Happening] The King is Dead, Long Live the King!: The old ruler is gone (assassinated? death faked? exiled?). The GM must determine who now sits the throne over the City. The players should expect changes from the new regime. XI [Rumor] The Sporehulk’s Wife: The Sporehulk is the dungeon lord of the Sepulcher. It is said that inside one of the chambers lies the barrow of his wife, around which is arranged four canopic jars containing her brains, her liver, her lungs, and her ovaries. If you eat any part of the Sporehulk’s wife, it’s said you’ll undergo a terrible and awesome transformation. XII [Rumor] The Star’s Daughter: A fallen star dwells on an island in the Boundless Moat, and his daughter came with him into exile. Both star-beings struggle adorably with human culture. The star wishes for someone to marry his daughter. As a dowry, the star will grant a wish to anybody who marries her. However, the daughter will interpret the wish. It would be wise to keep her happy unless you want the wish to go sour. XIII [Rumor] Medusa’s Abortion: A gorgon was recently slain in the Underworld, yet somehow its premature fetus survived. The awful, crawling, half-serpentine thing is gnawing its way through the Castle of Crossed Destinies. Even glancing at it turns you into stone. That’s why there are so many more statues in the Castle as of late. XIV [Rumor] The Strangler’s Palm: Inside a hidden room in the Castle of Crossed Destinies is a tavern—a haven for adventurers in the middle of the Worm’s own realm. If you can find it, 10g will purchase a safe place to encamp and some of the most exotic foods you’ve ever eaten. The password this month is “pickle juice.” XV [Rumor] The Tomb of the First Dead: Inside the City of Ruin is a graveyard. The first graveyard, in fact. It is called the Tomb of the First Dead, and it holds a mausoleum for the first human to ever succumb to the doom of old age and death. Inside this tomb is a treasure that will make you immune to the mental control of the three immortal nymphs that live within the Underworld. XVI [Travel event] A Theft: The adventurer in back of the marching order is bumped into by a louse- ridden orphan. Later, as they round a corner, they see a piece of gear that looks suspiciously like their own at a merchant’s stall. Several interested buyers are already taking notice. XVII [Travel event] A Challenge: A pair of bravos sitting outside of a wine sink make snide remarks about the clothes of the adventurer with the highest Pentacles score. They’re spoiling for a fight, though they’re more into humiliation than actual harm. XVIII [Travel event] A Proposition: Several whores call down compliments about the adventurer with the highest Wands score. They claim they’ll give them a discount, if the adventurer is so inclined. XIX [Travel event] An Inheritance: The adventurer with the lowest Cups score receives a letter from their family. A distant uncle has died and bequeathed them a townhouse by the Grey River, complete with a snooty butler named Aethelred that hates them. Though initially a boon, this townhouse will soon become the center of a web of intrigue that will haunt the guild. XX [Travel event] A Disaster: Fire! After step 6 (City Actions), the inn the guild is staying at catches fire. This prompts a test of Pentacles to escape quickly. If anybody fails, they leave behind the two items in the very bottom of their pack and begin the next Crawl with the Stressed condition. XXI [Signs and Portents] Strange Days: The GM notes the top card on the minor arcana discard pile and describes something from the Signs and Portents table (facing page).

478.title: Signs and Portents
478.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 3. City Events › Signs and Portents
478.body: Card Signs and Portents :---: --- I The Mushroom Forest: Yellow mushrooms with pink gills erupt from the flagstones of a random district. They stand as tall as columns, choking off traffic and commerce. That district’s special City Action cannot be used this City Phase. II The Blood-Red Star: A comet hangs over the City: a menstrual smear across the sky in both night and day. Its sickly red-brown light causes sleeplessness in the City. Everyone you meet is haggard and bleary eyed, barely holding onto sanity. You can’t sleep either. Begin the next Crawl Phase Stressed. III Mists: Emerald-colored fog rises out of the mouths to the Underworld, blotting out the sun. This phase takes place in an unnatural, unending night. IV The Ancient Quarter: A district of the City that hasn’t existed in centuries reappears from the mists of the ages. Its residents are antique and deeply confused about where they are and how they got here. Draw an additional district, per the rules in Appendix D: City Creation. This district becomes a part of the present City. V The Honey Cult: An adventurer brought black honey to the City. All who eat of it profess to see terrible and wonderful visions of a pregnant woman. They rave about the Nascent Horde. Something about their ravings causes a deep anxiety inside of you. VI Dreams: Dreams begin wandering through the City. A husband begins having the dreams of his wife. A hay merchant suddenly begins having the dreams of his neighbor, a clothier. The archbishop begins having dreams of the inbred princess locked in the Tower of Forbiddance. Each player must tell one secret to another player, which their adventurer dreams about. VII The Slime Catastrophe: Some thoughtless adventurer brought a baby green slime back into the City. It quickly grew in size, swallowing the food of the inn, the horses, the stables, and entire city blocks. Before it was vanquished with a fire, it ate an entire district. Remove one random district from the City. VIII Rip Van Winkle: Time moves strangely in the Underworld. You return to the City a full 100 years after you left. Your children are old and your lovers are dead. IX The Thing in the Water: Fishermen pull forth the corpse of some stupendous white thing from the waters of the Grey. The ocean sings a pitiful song for the next week. The song elicits a feeling of devastating ennui. Several named GM characters walk into the ocean and are never seen again. X Dog Suicide: All the dogs of the City commit suicide overnight: they throw themselves off of bridges, smash themselves through glass windows, drown themselves in the Grey. XI The Black Miracle of the Statues: Every graven image in the City begins speaking terrible blasphemies. In a fit of iconoclasm, the Cult begins smashing all representative art. Statues, paintings, idols, mosaics, figureheads, children’s toys, etc., are all fuel for their holy bonfires. Religious fervor is increased in the near term. XII The Blood Rain: Red clouds, swollen like pustules, begin raining blood. The blood flows in rivulets down the streets, pollutes cisterns, stains everything. It’s gross. XIII The Child of Silence: A giant infant crawls down the streets. The thing is surrounded with an aura of impenetrable silence: no sound whatsoever carries in its presence. It seems to be hunting the guild. The guild can hide and forestall this doom, though the Child of Silence will doubtless cause some terrible harm if left unchecked. XIV What Is Dead May Never Die: The dead haunt the City. Until the guild finds the source of the undead in the Underworld and quells it, no City Actions can be performed. If the plague of the dead is allowed to continue, the Underworld will breach onto the surface, devouring the City (as it has devoured so many cities before). Refer to this table when the City Events table yields a XXI result.

479.title: 4. Turn in contracts
479.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 4. Turn in contracts
479.body: Turn in any contracts completed during the Crawl Phase. Visit your quest-givers, report your successes (or failures), and receive any due rewards. This often gives you the coin you need to pay for upkeep. ^turn-in-contracts Turning in a contract gives 1XP per contract fulfilled. If there were no contracts completed, skip this step. As part of this step, adventurers may sell items of art and extravagance , such as gems, paintings, and jewelry. The GM determines the value of the items being sold when creating the Underworld; see How much treasure?. The seller receives any payments prior to paying their upkeep.

480.title: 5. Upkeep
480.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 5. Upkeep
480.body: Life in the City isn’t free. Upkeep pays for your food and lodging and refills your pack with adventuring gear. ^upkeep The cost for equipment isn’t itemized . Buying into a given upkeep tier buys you as much gear of that particular tier (or lower) as you can waddle away with. See the Omphalic Market for a list of adventuring gear . There are four upkeep tiers: destitute, impoverished , common , and luxurious . Upkeep --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Destitute - 0g If you can’t (or refuse) to pay upkeep, you sleep on the street. Dogs lick your wounds. You have nothing to eat and begin your next adventure Stressed.<br <br You cannot buy any new gear when you are destitute. Impoverished - 25g If you’re impoverished, you sleep in the poorhouse or in the common room of a cheap inn. You gain neither special benefits nor penalties.<br <br You can purchase as many pieces of gear from the impoverished item list as you can carry. Common - 50g Common lodgings afford you a stay in a decent inn. During this step, you may burn charged Bonds to heal Wounds and recover Resolve, just like step 4 (Recovery) of the Camp Phase (End of Camp Phase).<br <br You can purchase as many pieces of gear from the impoverished and common item lists as you can carry. Luxurious - 100g If you live in luxury and stay in the most high-class establishments, you fully heal every Wound and begin the Crawl with full Resolve.<br <br You can purchase as many pieces of gear from the impoverished, common, and luxurious item lists as you can carry.

481.title: 6. City Actions
481.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 6. City Actions
481.body: When you visit the City, you have some downtime in which to pursue your own interests. You might relax in the hot springs, track down the answers to thorny questions, or feed the poor. These activities are represented by City Actions . During each trip made to the City, each adventurer can perform one City Action. ^city-actions A list of common City Actions should be provided to the players by the GM. In general, the GM will assemble this list by combining the standard list of actions (found below) with a unique list of actions based on the districts of the City discovered by using the rules in Appendix D: City Creation, see The Districts. It would be impossible for the list of City Actions to be exhaustive. The City is the largest metropolis in the Wide World and, as such, just about anything is possible. Players, if you have a weird idea, ask your GM if it’s possible. GMs, use your common sense and this list to model new actions for your players. Note that most every action except for Beg and Busk requires lump sums of cash to initiate.

482.title: Banking
482.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 6. City Actions › Banking
482.body: Put that money away for a rainy day. Store your extra items and coin in Cult-run banks. - Every City Phase, your total gold investment has a 2% return on investment. - Your gear is safe .

483.title: Beg and Busk
483.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 6. City Actions › Beg and Busk
483.body: Sing for coin in streets and winesinks. - Draw from the minor arcana deck. You gain gold equal to the numerical value of your draw + Wands attribute.

484.title: Build
484.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 6. City Actions › Build
484.body: Invest your money to build something that will last. Something that will calcify and become the bones of the City itself. - Use this action to build statues and fountains, start a tavern, buy a house, or create other permanent structures in the City. - Talk to your GM about what you want. If it’s reasonable, the GM will tell you which artisan can design it for you. - Describe your project in a few words. The price for a building project equals 50 gold per syllable of the building’s description. Examples: buffoonish gargoyle that looks like your rival (550g), statue in a busy square (350g), church bell (100g), extravagant monastery (400g)

485.title: Camp Action
485.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 6. City Actions › Camp Action
485.body: Though somewhat smaller in scope than City Actions, any Camp Action (Camp Actions) can be performed as a City Action, e.g., Use a Talent, Use an Item, etc.

486.title: Carouse
486.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 6. City Actions › Carouse
486.body: Spend everything you earned on drinking and whoring. - If you spend 50% of the gold you brought back, you get 1XP . - If you spend 100% of the gold you brought back, you get 2XP . - In addition, the GM draws a major arcana and consults the Hangover table on the next page to see if there are any complications later. Carousing is an easy, micro-math way to get a meaningful benefit. It emulates genre staples of heroes like Conan or Fafhrd and the Gray Mouser frittering away last adventure’s booty and starting each story dead broke. Anything in brackets [ ] refers to the top card of the minor arcana discard pile. Sometimes brackets provide numerical values—for example, “\[value] in gold coins” provides a number of gold coins equal to the value of the card. Sometimes brackets provide a random result within the table’s entry based on the suit of the card. Card Hangover :---: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- I You awaken with a headache and [value] new gold coins in your pocket. II You awaken in the stocks, having been left there to sober up. A little bruised, but no worse for wear. Your guild has a chance to make fun of you and throw tomatoes before you’re let out. III A cowbell has been hung around your neck by a steel chain. The chain is too small to remove over your head, and you don’t have the key to the lock. You clang while you walk until you solve this problem. IV You awaken with a marriage ring on your finger, but no memory of who you married. V You awaken in a strange room, heavy pounding on the door. The people on the other side are very angrily demanding their money back. VI You awaken with a marriage ring on a finger. The finger isn’t yours. VII You awaken next to a [even] High Priest / [odd] High Priestess. They thank you for helping them break their vows, and showing them what it means to be happy. VIII You are thrown through the window of your usual watering hole. “And stay out!” the proprietor adds. You are banned from your favorite tavern. IX You awaken with a new tattoo. <br • The tattoo is on your: \[Swords] arm, \[Pentacles] leg, \[Cups] backside, \[Wands] face.<br • It is: \[1–2] horribly offensive, \[3–8] cringe and misspelled, \[9–King] pretty sweet. X You awaken in an alley. Hobos around you seem to be wearing your clothes and armor. But you’re wearing theirs, so… even trade? XI A letter is delivered to your room. It’s from a local aristocrat and they have accepted your invitation to a duel. The duel is in [value] days. XII You awaken in the muck of a cistern wearing only your smallclothes. All the other items you had on you are missing as well. XIII You don’t remember exactly what you did, but by the wanted posters lining the streets you can guess it wasn’t good. Choose based on the card’s suit: [Swords] armed robbery, [Pentacles] attempted pick-pocketing, [Cups] lewd acts, [Wands] consorting with dark entities. XIV You find an invoice in your pouch: “Sold: One (1) soul for one (1) beer.” Your signature and an infernal symbol seal the contract. XV You awaken to the sounds of sobbing. There seems to be a nobleman hogtied and gagged on your floor. How strange. XVI Why are you naked and wearing a fake bull’s head? Why does this shop have nothing but broken plates and smashed glass? Why are the shopkeeper and constables so angry and yelling? XVII Luckily, it only burns when you pass water. XVIII You back your way out of a blackout wrapped in a warm snuggly robe standing in a candle lit room. It’s nice. “The dark pact is complete,” a deep baritone voice says, “Go forth, my brothers, and see that our lord’s will be done.” ... Wait, what? XIX Where the hells is your hand? Why can you feel it crawling? XX You remember agreeing to a dare. It had something to do with a candle and flatulence. <br • You find that: <br \[Swords] a district is burnt down<br \[Pentacles] two districts are burnt down<br \[Cups] three districts are burnt down<br \[Wands] as Cups, but a fire spirit is still roaming the City, and the sorcerers are pissed. XXI Did you always have those circular puncture marks on your neck? I’m sure it’ll be fiiiine.

487.title: Commission Craft
487.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 6. City Actions › Commission Craft
487.body: Is there something you want that can’t be found in the Omphalic Market? Commission a bespoke version, all shiny and new. - Talk to your GM about what you want. If it’s reasonable, the GM will tell you which merchant can craft it for you. - Describe it in a few words. The price for a commissioned craft is as follows: - 1 gold per syllable of the commission if it’s something a farmer might have. Examples: scrimshaw pipe (3g), tricorn hat (3g), pan flute (2g), wooden dentures (4g) - 5 gold per syllable of the commission if it’s something an adventurer might have. Examples: helmet with a candle holder (40g), imp trap (10g), silverthread bug net (25g) - 10 gold per syllable of the commission if it’s something a noble might have. Examples: mirror masquerade mask (60g), cloth of gold gown (40g), lion-themed parade armor (70g), bespoke clothing (40g) - 25 gold per syllable of the commission if it’s something that nobody has—something brand new. Examples: prosthetic leg (100g), manticore saddle (125g), decorative harpy wings (175g) The fewer details you provide, the more details the GM will supplement. If you have a clear picture in mind, articulate what you want using the name of the item. No fair saying you want a “set of ten-foot mechanical articulate tongs” by just saying “Long tongs.” “Reasonableness” is up to the GM. We don’t really truck with steampunk machinery or firearms or whatever, but maybe your table is different. Assuming that the adventurer has an appropriate motif that establishes them as a craftsman, the adventurer can be the one actually making the item. The prices are the same: the gold is spent on renting a workshop and supplying raw materials.

488.title: Hold a Funeral
488.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 6. City Actions › Hold a Funeral
488.body: Haul your dead friends out of the Underworld and say some nice words over them. - That player’s new adventurer retains a portion of their previous adventurer’s XP. - Each 1XP reclaimed by the new adventurer costs 100 gold worth of funeral expenses.

489.title: Prepare Components
489.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 6. City Actions › Prepare Components
489.body: Barter with talismongers, engage in midnight rituals, and venture outside the City to gather herbs in the darkness of the new moon. When you use this action, fill your pack with as many spell components from Appendix A as you wish. Each component takes up one pack slot.

490.title: Research
490.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 6. City Actions › Research
490.body: Investigate a topic of your choice by spending money to pay bribes to librarians, buy coffee to stay awake during long reading sessions, and get people drunk enough to talk. - Spend 50 gold to test Cups. - On a success, you can ask the GM one question about any subject. - If you have a great success, you can ask three .

491.title: Support
491.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 6. City Actions › Support
491.body: Long-term projects The Support action is the main tool that players have to pursue longterm projects. If you speak Apocalypse World jargon, think about complexity like “clocks.” You can also think about it in terms of “hit points” that you need to tick off of a project before you’re successful. Each Support step is filled by spending gold. • 25 gold is enough to make a small impact. For example, a 25g donation to an orphanage may buy all the orphans a batch of new toys. • 50 gold can make a humble but meaningful impact. For example, 50g can patch the orphanage’s leaky roof. • 100 gold can make a significant impact. For example, 100g might be enough to make sure the orphans have enough to eat for a month. • 1000 gold is needed to make a truly dramatic statement. If you want to adopt all the orphans and provide for their care personally, you might need to spend up to 1000g. Some actions are one-and-done, e.g., you go gambling and lose your hard-earned coin all in a night. In contrast, Support involves taking one step on a long road. Use this action to represent long-term scheming on large, multistep projects. - Large projects are broken up into several steps. How many steps a project requires is determined by its complexity , as determined by the GM. The more complex a project, the more steps that it takes. - Complexity usually ranges between 2–8. Simple projects might only need two or three steps to complete, whereas complex ones need as many as eight. - You make one step toward project completion by spending money in a way that supports your goals. Players must suggest a way that they would spend their coin to benefit their goals. The GM must agree that this action will move the needle on their long-term project and set an appropriate price. - Once a player has fulfilled a number of steps equal to the project’s complexity, the project is complete.

492.title: Train
492.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 6. City Actions › Train
492.body: Seek out an expert and study under them. Talk to the GM about what talent you want to learn. The GM will tell you who is available to train you. - Spend 50 gold per 1XP you want to invest on the new talent. - Prepare as many uses of that talent as you have XP invested. - See Talents for full details about training talents.

493.title: 7. Plan the next Crawl
493.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 7. Plan the next Crawl
493.body: Once every player has resolved their City Action, the GM sets a role-playing scene in a tavern where the guild comes together to debrief, drink, and determine their next steps. ^plan-next-crawl Taverns have job boards where contracts are offered to guilds. These are jobs that characters in the City offer to guilds, with rewards of coin, peerage, rare items, or favors. During this step, the GM provides four to six potential contracts for the guild to consider. A guild merely needs to affix their seal to the contract to start pursuing it (Current Contracts). Role-play the conversation with your guild-mates and decide collectively what you want to do next. Did you complete your previous quest? What quest will you pursue next? Did you complete your previous contract? Are there any current contracts you want to pursue? Some example contracts are offered on the next page.

494.title: 8. Restock the Underworld
494.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 8. Restock the Underworld
494.body: Advice for Exploration-based Games “The adventure is in the wilderness, not the town. As per the discussion of NPCs [non-player characters] … be careful not to change the focus to urban adventure instead of exploration. You can have as many NPCs as you want in town, but remember it’s not about them. Once players start talking to town NPCs, they will have a perverse desire to stay in town and look for adventure there. ‘Town game’ was a dirty word in West Marches. … You find things by exploring, not sitting in town — someone who explores should know more about what is out there than someone in town.” - “Great Experiments: West Marches,” Ben Robbins The Underworld grows and shifts. Between the end of the City Phase and the start of the next session, the GM revisits their Meatgrinder and City Events tables and replaces any entries that the players have already encountered. If an ogre is slain, a hidden room looted, or a rusty trap sprung, replace those entries with something new. ^restock-underworld GMs should ask themselves: How has the Underworld been changed by the player’s actions? Factions will refill their posts. Other factions will move into cleared rooms. Other guilds meet with success or failure. The Underworld is dynamic, not static. Reflect the changing Underworld by adding new content to the Meatgrinder tables.

495.title: Example Contracts
495.breadcrumb: Chapter 9: The City Phase › The Flow of the City Phase › 8. Restock the Underworld › Example Contracts
495.body: Here are a few contracts that might be on a job board at your local tavern. Draw 5 cards to create a job board.
