By this token, an unattended weapon will only strike once per casting. - In a Challenge, the item’s action has the same value as the sorcerer’s Speak Incantation value. This spell lasts until the item fulfills its task. Resolve spent on casting this spell can never refresh as long as the spell continues.

617.title: Change Size
617.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Weird › Change Size
617.body: Component: A twine of tails from a rat king The sorcerer causes the target to either Shrink or Grow . A size-changed creature shrinks or grows to either half or double their original height. - When this would be advantageous (squeezing into holes, sneaking around ), they gain favor. - When this would be disadvantageous (contests of strength), they gain disfavor. - The size difference never affects Attack values, but might influence actions like Roughhouse. This spell is maintained with concentration.

618.title: Enrage
618.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Weird › Enrage
618.body: Component: A mummified viper The sorcerer weaves an illusion visible only to the target, causing them to perceive a second, willing target as a nebulous but hated foe. The primary target is Inspired with anger towards the illusion-cloaked creature. - In combat, anger makes people stupid and clumsy. The angry creature will try and focus on the source of their anger. An angry creature will attack recklessly, with little regard to the environment. - Creatures that do not feel emotions or are not affected by illusions are not affected by this spell. This spell is maintained with concentration, but any actions that would change the target’s Disposition also end this spell.

619.title: Give Form to Nothingness
619.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Weird › Give Form to Nothingness
619.body: Component: A drum made of the hide of an albino deer writ with runes The sorcerer plays the rune-painted drum as they cast the spell. All intangible or invisible entities or objects in that room become both tangible and visible. - This spell’s component, a drum, is standard size but requires two hands to play during Challenges. - Each additional Resolve spent allows the sorcerer to target one extra room. This spell lasts as long as the drum is played.

620.title: Illusion
620.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Weird › Illusion
620.body: Component: A seven-faceted prism The sorcerer creates an illusion of any object or creature. - The illusion is merely an image—a hologram—and has no weight or substance, creates no sound, no smells, etc. - Illusions are only additive, never subtractive. For example, something cannot be made unseen with an illusion, but an illusory wall could obscure it. Making something unseen is the purview of the Shroud spell. - The illusion obeys the sorcerer’s mental commands. During Challenges, this requires a miscellaneous action. This spell is maintained by concentration. While maintaining the spell, the sorcerer may add details to the illusion by spending 1 Resolve per detail. For example, they may elect for an illusion of a knight to pull a new item (such as a scroll or weapon) from its pack by spending 1 Resolve.

621.title: Mirror Meld
621.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Weird › Mirror Meld
621.body: Component: A vial of tears collected from dreaming children The sorcerer sprinkles the component on the surface of a mirror to create a portal into the mirror through which creatures or items may pass. - The person who steps into the mirror becomes just a reflection; they are only visible within the mirror. They see and hear everything said near the mirror, but cannot interact with the world . - The mirror must be large enough to allow entrance; a halfling can step into a relatively small mirror, whereas it must be truly large to accommodate a troll. Multiple creatures may inhabit the same mirror as reflections. - A creature dwelling in the mirror may exit at any time by stepping back through the mirror portal. - Items may be left in the mirror. They will be visible but intangible to the outside world. - If the mirror is broken, the reflected adventurers are shunted back into reality and take 2 Wounds . Items in the mirror are Destroyed when they return to reality. - Items “carried” in a mirror still take up pack slots due to magical weight. This spell persists until the creatures inside choose to leave or the mirror is broken.

622.title: Portable Hole
622.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Weird › Portable Hole
622.body: Component: A circle of hide, of a diameter no larger than nine inches, cut from a black calf sacrificed at midnight When the sorcerer speaks the incantation and places the circle of calfskin, it becomes an opening through any inanimate material. - While the spell is active, the circle is essentially a hole—a window—to the immediate other side of the inanimate material. This creates an opening through walls/doors/chests, through which things can pass. - This spell simply doesn’t function on living tissue. - Things that fit somewhere in the blurred line of living and unliving (silicon viruses, undead , and animate stone gargoyles) are left up to the discretion of the GM. - This spell never damages the actual integrity of the transposing surface. Even if a portable hole is placed in a strategic load bearing section, the structure itself remains whole. - If the inanimate material has no other “side,” a hole about a foot deep opens. Items placed in this hole are swallowed, but not damaged by, the surrounding material when the spell ends. This spell is maintained by concentration. When the spell ends, the window closes back into the component circle of calfskin.

623.title: Scry
623.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Weird › Scry
623.body: Component: A crystal ball The sorcerer peers into the crystal ball and can see one location that they have visited before. - By default, this spell only functions if the chosen location is in the same metaphysical area that the sorcerer is currently in—the same city, dungeon level, forest, etc. - The sorcerer can see a location outside their current metaphysical area by spending +1 Resolve. This spell is maintained with concentration.

624.title: Shroud
624.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Weird › Shroud
624.body: Component: The funerary winding-sheet of one who died by an elf’s arrow The sorcerer spreads the component sheet over the target. The target and everything they carry becomes Shrouded . - A Shrouded creature is impossible to see without the aid of magic or special senses. Typically, if a Shrouded creature stands still and stays quiet, they cannot be deliberately targeted by creatures that can’t see them. - If the Shrouded creature moves, those nearby may have a vague sense of their presence. All attempts to target them are made with disfavor. - Shrouded creatures make harmful actions with favor against creatures who can’t see them. The illusory magic required to hide something becomes confused and strained when the target interacts with visible objects . If the subject sharpens their sword, drinks a potion from their belt, or puts on a disguise, the invisibility is maintained. If the subject opens a door, fires an arrow at a foe, or ties a friend’s shoelaces together, an additional Resolve must be immediately spent to maintain the spell. This spell is maintained with concentration.

625.title: Sleep
625.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Weird › Sleep
625.body: Component: A pouch of powder made from crushed lotus seeds, sand, and wormwood The sorcerer takes a pinch of the component powder and blows it towards the target. The target falls under the influence of a supernatural soporific. - If not in a tense or dangerous situation, the subject takes the Knockout effect and can only be awoken with a sharp slap. - If cast with 4 Resolve, the target doesn’t age or require food while asleep. - If in a tense or dangerous situation (like combat), the target becomes drowsy and is Stunned .

626.title: Spells of the Welkin
626.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Welkin

627.title: Augury
627.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Welkin › Augury
627.body: Component: A copy of the Codex Sophia, the sacred book of the Mythric cult The sorcerer receives supernatural wisdom to intuit the meaning of signs and portents by practicing rhapsodomancy—a form of book-based divination. This allows them to avoid the consequences of failure or great failures by looking into the future and forestalling doom. If a test of fate would be called for and the sorcerer has time to consult a random page of the Codex Sophia and cast this spell, the GM draws a card for the test of fate instead of the player. Without showing it to the players, the GM describes the contents of the card as a parable from the Codex Sophia. - For example, the X of Swords might yield the description, “And it said that / a man, stabbed many times, lying face down / may be very wounded, or very dead. / His face is turned away.” - The sorcerer’s player uses their out-of-character knowledge of the iconography of the tarot to interpret these results in character. They are not allowed to use outside help (no checking your phone). - Once the spell has been cast, a member of the guild may choose to attempt the task or not. If the attempt is made, the GM reveals the card. - Because casting this spell technically happens before making the test of fate, the player who makes the attempt of the test may elect to spend a Resolve for favor. They may also push fate with this test as normal. - If the guild decides not to take a course of action based on the augury, the bound by fate rule is still obeyed. The card is discarded. That action would either be successful (or not) until the situation significantly changes.

628.title: Binding
628.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Welkin › Binding
628.body: Component: The finger bone of a holy person buried in sacred soil for a year When casting this spell, the sorcerer holds the component out as a ward and names one creature. Any creature(s) so named in the sorcerer’s sight are Rooted . - If the name is specific (“John Doe”) the spell affects everyone by this specific name. - If the name is generic (“human”) the spell affects every creature of that type. - Per the GM’s judgment, castings that are vague or confusing might create maleficence. - This continues until the sorcerer’s concentration is interrupted. Affected creatures cannot use Recover to clear this Effect. The spell must be countered or interrupted. This spell is maintained with concentration.

629.title: Charm
629.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Welkin › Charm
629.body: Component: Oils of myrrh burned in an ivory censer The sorcerer weaves an illusion visible only to the target , causing them to perceive a second, willing target as an undefined but trusted friend. The primary target is Inspired with trust towards the illusion-cloaked creature. - Creatures with the trust Disposition are not inclined to fight. If the situation obligates a fight without changing this Disposition, the creature might attempt to learn more about the guild’s prowess through nonlethal methods. - Creatures that do not feel emotions or are not affected by illusions are not affected by this spell. This spell is maintained with concentration, but any actions that would change the target’s Disposition also end this spell.

630.title: Circle of Protection
630.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Welkin › Circle of Protection
630.body: Component: Ashes from a venerated saint held in a small silver monstrance As preparation for casting, the sorcerer spends a watch sketching out a circle of protective runes with the ashes. This circle encompasses a radius of no more than 10’. When the sorcerer incants this spell, they select one of the far realms (Waste, Weald , Weird, or Welkin ). Creatures and spirits native to that far realm are unable to pass or harm those on the other side of the circle. - If the sorcerer traces the circle but does not incant to empower it, it is possible to use it as a “trap” for a spirit by casting the spell once the spirit unwittingly crosses into the runic circle. - Each additional Resolve spent allows the sorcerer to ban spirits from another far realm. This spell is maintained with concentration.

631.title: Feather
631.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Welkin › Feather
631.body: Component: A feather from a lamassu The target item or creature floats, its weight is reduced to that of a feather. - If falling, the target floats gently to the ground. A sorcerer may cast this spell quickly in response to falling, but must already have the component in their hand to do so. - If moving across a surface, the target takes no damage from hazardous scenery ( like spikes) and will not trigger pressure-plate traps. - Heavy objects become easy to move. This spell is maintained with concentration.

632.title: Guardian Angel
632.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Welkin › Guardian Angel
632.body: Component: A vial of water collected by a virgin from a sacred spring When the sorcerer casts this spell, they summon an invisible minor welkin spirit known as a guardian angel. The sorcerer binds this guardian angel to a target to protect them from a single blow. - During Challenges, the sorcerer hands the target the card used for Speak Incantation. This card is placed facedown in front of the target player. At their discretion, they can flip the card up and use its value to either Dodge or Riposte . - The defensive action’s total value is cumulative with other actions of the same type. For example, if a player has a facedown Dodge and the Guardian Angel card is used to Dodge, the two actions values will be added together. - This spell does not count towards the limit of one facedown card per player. However, you cannot have multiple instances of this spell at the same time. This spell lasts until used.

633.title: Heavenfire
633.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Welkin › Heavenfire
633.body: Component: A votive candle made of the rendered fat of a sacrificed bull The sorcerer summons a gout of heavenfire towards the target. Heavenfire is a bright flame that burns with light but no heat. It does not consume whatever it is burning. - If cast on a living, sighted target , the sudden light Blinds them for a few moments. - In a Challenge, this lasts until the end of their next turn. - If cast on the undead or a spirit of the Wastes, this spell deals Piercing damage. - If cast on an object , it glows with bright light. - Because heavenfire does not create heat, the sorcerer can light the tip of their wand or their hat to provide light. - Items lit with heavenfire go out when a torches gutter result is drawn on the Meatgrinder table . - Heavenfire acts (in most ways) like normal flame. It can be extinguished through water or lack of oxygen.

634.title: Life
634.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Welkin › Life
634.body: Component: A feather from a phoenix This spell has no effect on living and otherwise-healthy creatures. However, if cast on someone who is at Death’s Door, they clear that condition . That person then takes the Stressed condition. - If cast on an afflicted creature , this spell reduces the progress of the affliction by one stage. If this would cure the first stage of affliction, the affliction is removed (Afflictions). - If cast on the undead , they suffer a Wound . - If cast on a plant, it Grows very quickly. - Each additional Resolve spent allows the sorcerer to add another target.

635.title: Seal Pact
635.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Welkin › Seal Pact
635.body: Component: A bag of goblin teeth and finger joints The sorcerer uses this spell to magically seal a contract or oath made by two willing parties. - If a party to the oath ever violates the terms of the pact, two things happen: - All other parties to the oath are immediately aware of the violation; and - The violator becomes doomed: at the absolutely most crucial moment in the future, they will automatically suffer a great failure when testing fate. - Being doomed isn't necessarily a death sentence, but taken in concert with disgruntled parties, it often is. - Additional parties may be added to the pact for +1 Resolve per person. This spell is permanent unless it is dispelled. Dispelling this spell triggers the first consequence but not the second. Once the pact is violated, however, these magical consequences cannot be dispelled or removed by any means. Lo! I unfold my darkness: and on This rock, place with strong hand the Book Of eternal brass, written in my solitude. – Book of Urizen, William Blake

636.title: Veritas
636.breadcrumb: Appendix A: Sorcery › Spells of the Welkin › Veritas
636.body: Component: Sacramental wine made of rare grapes in a golden ciborium When cast on a person, the sorcerer knows if the target knowingly tells a lie. - While under the effect of the spell, the target understands that they are essentially hooked up to a magical polygraph. This spell is maintained with concentration.

637.title: Appendix B: Alchemy
637.body: “That night the King walked late in his chamber in the Iron Tower alone. His jars and flasks and bottles of blue and green and purple glass wherein he kept his cursed drugs and electuaries of secret composition, his athals and athanors, his crucibles, his horsebellied retorts and alembics and bainsmaries, stood arow on shelves coated with dust and hung about with the dull spider's weavings... The King was deep in his contemplation, with a big black book open before him on the six-sided reading-stand: the damnablest of all his books, the same which had taught him aforetime what he must do when by the wicked power of enchantment he had wanted but a little to have confounded Demonland and all the lords thereof in death and ruin.” – The Worm Ouroboros, E. R. Eddison Alchemists are thieves. They are thieves of the worst sort. They steal souls . By butchering out the gallbladder, the liver, the bufonite, the alchemist distills the essence of a creature. This can only be done in death, of course, because death releases the soul. Distilling these reagents creates an alchemically reactive substance. This allows the alchemist to use the powers of monsters. At least, for a while. You can see why this is a vicious cycle.

638.title: The Alchemist’s Tools
638.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › The Alchemist’s Tools
638.body: There are two essential tools that the alchemist requires: an alchemy kit and hermetic bottles . An alchemy kit is a luxurious item that takes up 2 slots in your pack. It is a laboratory distilled down to its essentials: athanors, retorts, and alembics all wrapped up in a compact traveling case. An alchemy kit is needed for the Brew Alchemy Camp Action (see facing page). Hermetic bottles are common items that each take up one slot in your pack. Hermetic bottles seal tight, keeping both reagents and alchemical substances safe and potent. You must immediately brew each alchemical reagent you harvest into a substance or seal it in a hermetic bottle for preservation. In essence, the number of reagents/substances you can carry equals the number of empty hermetic bottles you have. (See the Omphalic Market, for details on equipment.)

639.title: Reagents
639.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › The Alchemist’s Tools › Reagents
639.body: Those strange creatures that dwell in the Underworld are alchemically potent. Their guts are, anyway. Adventurers with the Alchemy talent know which viscera have alchemical properties and can spend a watch to harvest these reagents . When you harvest a reagent and store it in a hermetic bottle, write down the reagent and the type of the creature it was harvested from like this: - Hermetic bottle: Eyes of salamander - Hermetic bottle: Toes of dire bat - Hermetic bottle: Tongue of hellhound Usually, any given creature can only produce one viable reagent. Huge monsters (elephant-sized or larger) might produce several. The GM will tell you what kind of reagents and how many can be harvested from a corpse. Reagents can only be harvested from freshly killed creatures. Creatures that have sat for a watch or more lose their alchemical properties to rot and spoilage. Similarly, harvested reagents that are stored outside of a hermetic environment cannot be used to brew alchemical substances. They rot too quickly.

640.title: What can be harvested?
640.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › The Alchemist’s Tools › Reagents › What can be harvested?
640.body: Creatures in the Underworld are inherently magical. It is this magic that alchemists exploit. Only monstrous creatures provide reagents . Some monsters yield no reagents. A wraith, for example, has no guts . A magically animated statue has no guts. No guts = no reagents . The GM makes the call on edge cases (“Is the blood on a bloodybones alchemically reactive?”), but in general this will be obvious to everyone. Sentient humanoids like humans, orcs, elves, or underfolk never provide reagents.

641.title: Brew Alchemy
641.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › The Alchemist’s Tools › Brew Alchemy
641.body: Anyone with the Alchemy talent and an alchemy kit can Brew Alchemy as a Camp Action. When you brew alchemy, you can turn reagents into alchemical substances . - You transform as many reagents at the same time as you want. - Each reagent is directly transformed into one alchemical substance. - You choose how to transform each reagent. Eyes of salamander can be turned into a bomb at the same time as you turn the toes of dire bat into a potion and the tongue of hellhound into an oil. At the end of the brew alchemy action, the alchemical substance replaces the reagent in the hermetic bottle. Erase the reagent and write the substance’s name like this: - Hermetic bottle: Salamander bomb - Hermetic bottle: Dire bat potion - Hermetic bottle: Oil of hellhound

642.title: Alchemical Substances
642.body: Forcing a potion down someone’s throat It is really hard to get someone to drink something they don’t want to. A potion is probably about the size of a glass of wine. Imagine holding one of your friend’s mouth open and trying to get them to swallow a glass of wine. Can it be done? In the right conditions. Can it be done easily? No. There are three types of alchemical substances. Potions (P) are beneficial or transformational when drunk. A sip of a potion is enough to produce the tiniest effect that might hint at the bottle’s contents. Drinking the entire bottle gives you the full effect. Bombs (B) are thrown in combat, exploding into a reactive spume of smoke and chemicals. This destroys the hermetic bottle. Bombs are almost always harmful or debilitating. Each bomb only affects a single target. During a Challenge, bomb effects are usually removed with the Recover action. Oils (O) have an effect on the environment. They can be poured out, slathered onto items, or have things dipped into them to create these effects. During Challenges, the Use Item Cups action is required to use any alchemical substance, whether that’s drinking a potion, throwing a bomb, or applying an oil (Cups actions).

643.title: Alchemical effects
643.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › Alchemical Substances › Alchemical effects
643.body: Alchemy bundles up a monster’s abilities and sticks them into a bottle. When you use an alchemical substance, you’re using a monster’s ability. Drink a potion to gain a dire spider’s wall climbing ability. Throw a bomb to poison a foe with the spider’s venom. Distill the spider’s webbing into a glue-like oil that bonds together whatever it touches.

644.title: Who does alchemy affect?
644.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › Alchemical Substances › Alchemical effects › Who does alchemy affect?
644.body: Potions only affect creatures with living processes. If you have blood, if you breathe, if you eat food, potions affect you. Creatures like the undead and automatons can neither benefit from nor be harmed by potions. Bombs are usually chemically reactive with the air around them, creating fires, acid, webs, vines, etc. These substances affect both creatures and the environment, unless the GM makes a call otherwise. Oils are chemical compounds that can make what they touch sticky, slippery, hot, invisible, etc. These substances affect whatever they touch, be it living or unliving, unless the GM makes a call otherwise.

645.title: Creating alchemical effects
645.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › Alchemical Substances › Creating alchemical effects
645.body: It is the GM’s job to determine what alchemical effects each creature can confer. Not every monster produces potions and oils and bombs. Sometimes a creature might only be able to produce a potion. Tell players this up front when they harvest a creature’s reagents. For creatures included in Appendix C, the GM’s task is relatively straightforward. We’ve included example substances for these monsters below. For creatures of the GM’s own invention, a little thought and inventiveness is needed.

646.title: Some advice for GMs:
646.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › Alchemical Substances › Creating alchemical effects › Some advice for GMs:

647.title: Steal the creature’s powers
647.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › Alchemical Substances › Creating alchemical effects › Some advice for GMs: › Steal the creature’s powers
647.body: When an adventurer harvests reagents, look at the creature’s stats and choose a few greater dooms that seem relevant and easy to convert for an adventurer’s benefit. - If the creature has an essential gimmick, it makes sense to include that gimmick as a potion. Example: A mermaid’s spleen can yield a potion of waterbreathing. - Potions might also provide a meaningful defense against a monster’s essential gimmick. Example: A medusa’s snakes can yield a potion that makes the drinker immune to petrification for a watch. - Does the monster have a signature attack? Seems like a good mechanic to tie to a bomb. Example: A dragon’s gallstone can yield a bomb that creates a fiery blast with the Critical effect.

648.title: Alchemy only lasts for a watch
648.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › Alchemical Substances › Creating alchemical effects › Some advice for GMs: › Alchemy only lasts for a watch
648.body: Generally, a substance’s effect only lasts for a watch—no longer. Unless an effect is minor or restores a natural state, it will eventually wear off.

649.title: Disregard balance, embrace creativity
649.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › Alchemical Substances › Creating alchemical effects › Some advice for GMs: › Disregard balance, embrace creativity
649.body: “Encounter balance” is not a meaningful concept in His Majesty the Worm. - If the players manage to defeat a strong creature, part of the reward is to gain strong alchemy from its corpse. - Because alchemical substances are single-use items, powerful effects are a fun lark and have little longterm effect on a game.

650.title: Keep good ideas, discard the rest
650.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › Alchemical Substances › Creating alchemical effects › Some advice for GMs: › Keep good ideas, discard the rest
650.body: When inventing alchemical effects, write out all of your ideas. Sift through them. Delete the ones that don’t seem to work. Keep the ones that do. - Some monsters will produce identical effects. That’s okay. - Some monsters will produce almost identical effects but a little bit better. That’s okay too.

651.title: What do players know about alchemy?
651.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › Alchemical Substances › Creating alchemical effects › What do players know about alchemy?
651.body: The GM should not tell players what alchemical effects can be obtained from a monster until they brew alchemy. The mystery is part of the fun. Can a player read this chapter and get a sense of the alchemical substances derived from the creatures in Appendix C? Of course. They can read a book. We’re not cops. Reading this book still does not reveal the alchemical effects for monsters that the GM invents themselves. There are two exceptions: - Bidding lore: If an adventurer has a pertinent motif (e.g., Big Nerd Alchemist or Wizened Dragon Eater), they may bid lore to ask about a particular monster’s alchemical substances. Each lore bid is a single question. That is, each lore bid reveals a single way that a reagent may be brewed: what are the effects of this monster’s potion, what are the effects of this monster’s bomb, etc. - Rumor mill: Discovery is fun, pretending that you don’t know something isn’t. The rumor mill (Chapter 6: The Crawl Phase) ensures that players don’t have to spin their wheels discovering something twice. If a guild learns about the alchemical effects of X, Y, and Z, the rumor mill allows them act on that information in-character in the future. Even in this case, though, the GM isn’t the one revealing this information. The adventurers simply have a justification for knowing what they know outof-character. The players are responsible for tracking and remembering this information.

652.title: A Sampling of Alchemical Substances
652.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances
652.body: A list of example substances for the monsters in Appendix C can be found below. Effects mentioned here, like Rooted and Controlled, are defined see Effects.

653.title: Brain spider
653.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances › Brain spider
653.body: Potions (P):When you speak, your brain literally hums and vibrates with psionic radiance. Anybody who hears you can understand your speech—even if you don’t share a language—because the meaning of your words is psychically broadcast. Bomb (B): The bomb explodes into a silver web that covers the victim, Rooting them. This silver web also affects incorporeal creatures. Oil (O): The chemicals in the brain spider’s spinnerets form a powerful glue. For a watch, this glue sticks two things inseparably together .

654.title: Cockatrice
654.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances › Cockatrice
654.body: Bomb (B): Cockatrices devour their petrified victims using a special stone-dissolving gland in their throat. Distill this gland to create this bomb. The bomb creates a blast of smoke that has one of the following effects depending on the target: - Destroys an item made of stone roughly the size of a person. - Melts a hole in a larger stone item, such as a stone door. - Deals Critical damage to a creature made of stone like a gargoyle or animate statue. Oil (O):Whatever stone this oil touches becomes fleshy. Pouring the oil onto a petrified creature permanently cures the Curse of petrification . It also makes stone walls gross.

655.title: Devil
655.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances › Devil
655.body: Potions (P): You are now immune to fire for a watch. Your gear is still affected normally. Bomb (B): The victim is Controlled to confess their gravest sin. Oil (O): This oil burns with an invisible fire . It casts no light but generates heat, like an ethanol fire in daylight. - This fire acts like a normal fire, consuming flammable items of wood, cloth, paper, etc. - If you dip a metal weapon (like a sword) into it, it burns as hot as a torch but sheds no light. Your weapon suffers a Notch, but your attacks might be especially deadly to creatures who are weak to fire. - The fire is not quenched by water. It can only be quenched by smothering.

656.title: Face rat
656.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances › Face rat
656.body: Potions (P): An illusion covers you that makes you look like a duplicate of the first creature you see after drinking this potion. This illusion lasts for a watch. - Illusions are purely visual, like a hologram. - Creatures that are not affected by illusions can see through this effect. Bomb (B): A face rat’s saliva rapidly grows dermis, which is used to create this bomb. The target’s ears, eyes, and mouth are immediately covered in skin: they are Blinded, Deafened , and Silenced . Each effect must be Recovered from separately; one Recover cures Blind, one Recover action cures Deafen, etc.

657.title: Fungoid
657.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances › Fungoid
657.body: Potion (P): You are immediately Healed . Tiny mushrooms sprout on your skin where your wounds once were. Bomb (B): The bomb explodes into a choking cloud of spores. Assuming the target breathes, they cough so badly they are Exhausted . This effect lasts until the victim performs a Recover action. Oil (O): A thick patch of huge mushrooms sprout wherever the oil is poured. The top card of the minor arcana discard pile determines the type of mushrooms: -

658.title: Griffin
658.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances › Griffin
658.body: Potion (P): The lion is the king of beasts but the griffin is the king of birds. When you drink this potion, a dungeon bird will seek you out, arriving in a watch or so. The dungeon bird will tell you a rumor. - These are similar to the rumors you hear in the City (City Events). - Dungeon birds look like owls but are not owls. The owls are not what they seem. Oil (O): The tear ducts of the griffin are harvested to create this oil. It cleans anything it touches. Rust, minor flaws, impurities, and filth slide off and vanish. This can be used to take an impromptu “dungeon bath.”

659.title: Harpy
659.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances › Harpy
659.body: Potion (P): Your arms become wings for a watch. You can fly but can’t hold anything. You cannot hover and must continue flying to stay in the air. Bomb (B): The target suffers the Inspire distaste in its victim. The victim hates the first creature they see. Lasts for a watch. Creatures that do not feel emotions are not affected by this alchemy.

660.title: Imp
660.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances › Imp
660.body: Potion (P): You vomit and are cured of any poisons or alchemical effects . During Challenges, you are also Exhausted until you take the Recover action. Bomb (B): You don’t want to know what part of the imp is used to create this bomb. The target is covered in a terrible stink. They are Stunned as they choke and cough. If they are an adventurer, they are also Stressed until they can wash off. Oil (O): Whatever this oil touches becomes utterly frictionless . If poured out, it creates a slippery puddle with a 10’ diameter.

661.title: Jinn
661.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances › Jinn
661.body: Potion (P): This potion is made from the jinn’s smokeless fire. When you drink it, you become Shrouded . You can also see all Shrouded creatures . However, this effect ends as soon as you interact with a visible object. - A Shrouded creature is impossible to see without the aid of magic or special senses. Typically, if a Shrouded creature stands still and stays quiet, they cannot be deliberately targeted by creatures that can’t see them. - If the Shrouded creature moves, those nearby may have a vague sense of their presence. All attempts to target them are made with disfavor. Bomb (B): Derived from the eyes of the jinn, this bomb explicitly affects intangible creatures. Intangible creatures are forced into the material realm, making them both visible and tangible . Oil (O): When poured onto the ground, this oil opens a fiery hole in reality . Anyone that enters it is teleported to the City, rocketing out of a manhole. A City Phase begins. This portal is open for about one minute.

662.title: Kelpie
662.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances › Kelpie
662.body: Potion (P): Gills etch themselves on your neck, like the Mariner from Waterworld. You can breathe underwater for a watch. Oil (O): The kelpie walks on water using a secretion in its hooves. Whatever this oil touches rejects water for a watch. - If poured onto water, this potion forms an island of oil about 10’ in diameter—the island is soft but sturdy enough to be used as a platform. - If an object is covered in the oil, it will not sink no matter what—it can’t even be pushed forcibly under water. - If you pour this on your boots, you can walk on water for a watch.

663.title: Mimic
663.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances › Mimic
663.body: Potion (P): You can talk to objects for the next three minutes in real time (use a stopwatch). - Objects know a lot about the tasks they were created to perform. - Spears regularly quote Sun Tzu, mugs can tell you a liquid’s alcohol content, etc. - Objects know a lot about what they’ve done. - Swords know who they’ve killed; doors have a good description of people who have opened them, etc. - Objects usually don’t know about a lot else. - If you give the GM a beer, the object is particularly talkative. You can talk to the object for as long as the GM is drinking your beer. Oil (O): If smeared on a non-living object, that object instantly becomes a mimic . The mimic is not loyal to you in any way.

664.title: Nymph
664.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances › Nymph
664.body: Potion (P): You become extremely beautiful . Tests of fate to favorably influence the Disposition of creatures that would be attracted to you are made with favor (Example test of fate with favor). You also cannot be Inspired or Controlled . These effects last for a watch. Bomb (B): The victim falls in love with the first creature they see. This is as though they have been Inspired with joy , except it’s romantic. This effect lasts for a watch. Creatures that do not feel emotions are not affected by this alchemy.

665.title: Ogre
665.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances › Ogre
665.body: Potion (P): You become immune to poisons for a watch. In fact, nothing you eat or swallow hurts you at all. You can swallow live coals, the One Ring, or shards of glass to no ill effect. Bomb (B): The victim emits a terrible, rage-inducing pheromone. All creatures in the same zone as the target are Inspired with anger towards the target . - In combat, anger makes people stupid and clumsy. The angry creature will try and focus on the source of their anger. An angry creature will attack recklessly, with little regard to the environment. - Creatures that do not feel emotions are not affected by this bomb. Oil (O): The ogre can famously digest anything. Their digestive acids can be distilled into a universal solvent . This oil can break down any adhesive and makes materials soft and pliable: stone becomes mud, metal becomes bendable, wood becomes paper.

666.title: Questing beast
666.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances › Questing beast
666.body: Potion (P): You can ask the GM about the location of any one person, place, or thing . The GM will answer your adventurer with a sudden flash of prophetic insight. Oil (O): Whatever the oil touches begins to emit a sound like the barking of many dogs. Draw twice on the Meatgrinder table. Any encounters drawn have noticed the sound and are headed to this area to check it out. This effect lasts for a watch.

667.title: Slime
667.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances › Slime
667.body: Potion (P): Your bones stop being bones and become fluid-filled sacs for a watch. You take no damage from falls for the duration. You can also squeeze your body through any space you can reach your hand through during this time, e.g., through a portcullis or into a mouse hole. Bomb (B): The bomb explodes in a spray of neon-green acid ooze that covers the target. Any armor the target is wearing is Destroyed . Oil (O): Slime oil is a powerful acid that can eat through any non-magical material except for glass, creating a hole about 5’ in diameter. It will eat through the floor. - Destroys any non-magical object it touches. - Deals Critical damage if it comes into contact with flesh.

668.title: Titan
668.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances › Titan
668.body: Potion (P): Your body quickly swells and you suddenly Grow . This effect lasts for a watch. - When this massive size would be advantageous to tests of fate (e.g., contests of strength, lifting gates), gain favor. When this would be disadvantageous to tests of fate (e.g., squeezing into holes, sneaking around), gain disfavor. - Your massive size does not provide favor to Challenge Actions. Oil (O): Whatever the oil is smeared on becomes ten times as heavy . This doesn’t create any structural problems for the object itself (statues don’t collapse under their own weight, for instance) but can create structural problems for the environment around it.

669.title: Ungoat
669.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances › Ungoat
669.body: Potion (P): You cannot be targeted with spells (as if you’re wearing iron armor) for a watch. You also cannot cast spells. Bomb (B): The target immediately draws on a random Maleficence table. Whatever effect occurs is centered on the target. Oil (O): The oil negates any active spells affecting the thing it's smeared on for a watch. - This can pause permanent enchantments on objects for a watch (e.g., the flaming sword is just a regular sword). - This instantly ends active spells that sorcerers are concentrating on.

670.title: Vampire
670.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances › Vampire
670.body: Potion (P): You transform into a thick mist . Your equipment drops to the ground. This lasts for a watch. - You can move at a walking pace in your mist form. - You can move freely through small cracks, under doors, through keyholes, etc. - Most attacks and environmental hazards cannot harm you. The GM can make a ruling if certain circumstances (e.g., strong winds, super cold temperatures) provide any problems. Bomb (B): The target suffers all of the vampire’s weaknesses for a watch. They become Stunned whenever they are exposed to sunlight, wholesome herbs (e.g., garlic, wolfsbane, or wild rose), silver, or running water.

671.title: Winter wolf
671.breadcrumb: Appendix B: Alchemy › A Sampling of Alchemical Substances › Winter wolf
671.body: Potion (P): You become immune to cold temperatures and ice-based damage for a watch. You can stand outside in a blizzard in your small clothes comfortably. Oil (O): As soon as the oil touches air, it begins to freeze . - Will freeze a body of water the size of an Olympic swimming pool. - If poured onto the ground, it forms a wall of ice 10’ tall, 10’ wide, 1’ thick. Walls of ice are opaque and impermeable. “The substance was the pyromancers’ own term for wildfire. They called each other wisdom as well, which Tyrion found almost as annoying as their custom of hinting at the vast secret stores of knowledge that they wanted him to think they possessed. Once theirs had been a powerful guild, but in recent centuries the maesters of the Citadel had supplanted the alchemists almost everywhere. Now only a few of the older order remained, and they no longer even pretended to transmute metals . . . but they could make wildfire.” – A Clash of Kings, George R. R. Martin

697.title: Gamemaster Content
697.body: By default, search and the contents list show only player-facing content. To prevent any accidental spoilers the Gamemaster’s half of the book — Chapter 10 (The Worm Turns) and Appendices C, D, and E, where dungeon denizens, city creation, and the making of the underworld live — is opt-in. Nothing there is necessarily forbidden reading. But if you’re a player, the underworld is better met in play: its monsters, treasures, and secrets are your Gamemaster’s to reveal. If you run the game — or you’ve talked it over with your table and want to read on anyway — opt in below. The choice is remembered for this game only, and you can change it any time from the contents.
